newsitem.title: FRANCE: Princess Stephanie's husband wants inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Princess Stephanie's husband wants inquiry.

text.p: The husband of Monaco's Princess Stephanie will not fight a divorce after being snapped on a sex romp with a Belgian stripper, but he wants a court to investigate whether he was framed, his lawyer said on Tuesday.

"Our goal is to protect the children," lawyer Guillaume Carre said, explaining why his client Daniel Ducruet would not contest the divorce initiated by the princess after Italian magazines printed graphic photographs of him cavorting with a former "Miss Topless Belgium", 26-year-old Fily Houteman.

Carre said Ducruet hoped he would be granted extensive rights to visit the couple's two children, Louis and Pauline, aged three and two, after the divorce becomes final in an estimated three to five weeks.

The French daily France-Soir reported on Tuesday that the couple had agreed that Ducruet, the princess's ex-bodyguard and a former fish merchant, would be paid a monthly allowance of 15,000 francs ($3,000) after the divorce.

Carre said he would file a lawsuit by the weekend in a French court on Ducruet's behalf, asking a judge in the Riviera capital of Nice to look into how paparazzi knew ahead of time that Ducruet and Houteman would be at a private Riviera villa.
The suit, to be filed against unnamed defendants, will enable Ducruet to learn whether the photographs "were an accident or not", Carre told Reuters, speculating that his client was set up.

The photographs were taken in Cap de Villefranche, some 15 km (nine miles) from Monte Carlo. Ducruet, a keen racing driver, met Houteman during a race in Belgium and photographers had been on their trail ever since.

"It was certainly not my client who called in the photographers. And given the repercussions, we have the right to ask questions that an investigating magistrate will now have the task of answering," Carre said.

The French weekly L'Evenement du Jeudi has reported that Ducruet was likely framed by the Italian Mafia, whose interests in the principality were threatened by Ducruet's business activities. There has been no confirmation of the report.

The Italian magazine Eva Tremila and its sister publication Gente printed dozens of pages of explicit pictures of Houteman undressing Ducruet, the pair entwined on a sunbed and finally both naked by a poolside.
The principality banned the magazines but copies circulated widely and a video was reported to be on sale at the nearby Italian border town of Ventimiglia.

The video "proves everything and hides nothing," the French daily Le Monde said. Le Monde columnist Pierre Georges said the royal family had been "caught in a trap of its own making, having systematically auctioned off photo albums on any and every occasion".

Stephanie, 31, is the glamorous daughter of Prince Rainier and the late Hollywood screen goddess Grace Kelly who was killed in a car crash in 1982. She launched divorce proceedings after an unsuccessful reconciliation meeting on Sunday.

The princess wrote to her father, as ruler of the tiny Riviera principality, requesting the divorce. He was expected to refer the suit to the Monaco court of revision, her lawyer Thierry Lacoste said in a brief statement.
The latest upheaval in the Monaco royal family came just before the Grimaldi family celebrates 700 years in power next year, claiming to be the longest-serving European royal dynasty.
Prince Rainier long opposed Stephanie's relationship with Ducruet but finally accepted him into the family last year for the sake of the couple's children.
